title: What decides your finish date?
principle: Find the critical path. Buy ready-made things if making them could delay you.

screens.text: Let me tell you about the Delhi Metro. In India, big building projects were often years late. But the Delhi Metro finished its first part in 2005, two years and nine months early, without spending more than planned. Can you guess how?

screens.prompt: What do you think helped the Delhi Metro finish so early?

options.label: It worked at its sites day and night
It made all the parts on its own
It checked each day's work against its plan

screens.why: Its chief, E. Sreedharan, checked every deadline each day. Instead of waiting to learn how to make trains, it bought the first trains ready-made from South Korea. Later trains were finished in India by BEML, an Indian company.

screens.title: The critical path
screens.text: Some jobs must wait for others: first buy flour, then bake, then pack. These jobs form a chain. The longest chain is your critical path, and it decides when you finish. Making other jobs faster won't help. If a job on this chain is slow, buy it ready-made.

screens.title: Now look at your bakery
screens.text: A metro and a wedding cake both have a date that cannot change. It's November, the fifth year of your home bakery, and wedding season. A family wants a three-tier cake and 200 cupcakes for 28 November. You can do some jobs together, but others must wait.

screens.prompt: Chain 1: stands from Mumbai, 10 days. Chain 2: design approval, 3 days, then test cake, 2 days. Both start together. Which sets your date?
screens.why: Exactly. Both chains run at the same time, so the longer one decides when you finish. The stands take 10 days. That's your critical path. Making the test cake faster won't help the order finish earlier.

wrong.a: Chain 2 takes 3 + 2 = 5 days. But the stands take 10 days. Both chains start together, so the longer one decides when you finish.
wrong.c: You would add the days only if one chain had to wait for the other. Here, both run together. So the longer chain, 10 days, decides when you finish.

screens.prompt: Your past Mumbai orders took 10, 12 and 13 days. The shop promises 10 days. How many days should you plan for?
screens.why: Right. A writer named Douglas Hofstadter gave this idea a name: things take longer than you plan, even when you allow for delays. Plan for the longest time you've seen, and keep some extra days if you can.

wrong.a: That's what the shop promises. But your past orders took 10, 12 and 13 days. Plan for the longest time you've seen: 13 days.
wrong.b: If you planned for 12 days, one of your three past orders would have been late. The longest took 13 days, so plan for 13. Things can take longer than you expect.

screens.prompt: Here are five steps to plan a big order, but they're mixed up. Put them in the right order.
steps: Write down every job needed for the order
Mark which jobs must wait for other jobs
Add the days needed for each chain of jobs
Find the longest chain, called the critical path
Keep extra days, and buy ready-made things that could delay you
screens.why: Exactly. First, list all the jobs and find which ones must wait. Then find the longest chain. Keep extra days, because work can take longer than planned. If making something on your critical path could delay you, buy it ready-made.

screens.setup: It's 15 November. The wedding is in 13 days. Stands from Mumbai cost ₹900 and took 10 to 13 days before. No nearby shop sells them, but one will rent them to you today for ₹1,500. That's ₹600 more.
screens.question: How do you plan the wedding order?

options.label: Order from Mumbai and bake the cupcakes early
options.outcome: The cupcakes are ready by 20 November. The stands arrive on the 27th, the night before the wedding. The cupcakes are now a week old, so you bake all 200 again. That costs about ₹3,000 more, while you spend the whole night decorating three tiers.
options.why: You finished the cupcakes early, but they weren't on the critical path, so the order couldn't finish sooner. You still had to wait for the stands.
options.better: Rent the stands nearby today, and buy your own later.

options.label: Order from Mumbai and save ₹600 on stands
options.outcome: The stands arrive on day 12, the evening before the wedding. You spend the night decorating. The cake is ready, but one tier leans to one side, and you fix it at the wedding hall an hour before the guests arrive.
options.why: You saved ₹600, but you kept no extra days for the slowest job. The stands almost made you late.
options.better: Rent the stands nearby today, and buy your own later.

options.label: Rent stands nearby and pay ₹600 more today
options.outcome: You get the stands today. The test cake is ready by the 20th, and the family says yes to it. You bake the cupcakes two days before the wedding, and the cake is ready a day early. In January, when there's no rush, you order your own stands from Mumbai.
options.why: Exactly. You paid ₹600 more to take the slowest job off your critical path, so now you have extra days. Buy ready-made things when making or waiting for them could delay you. You can buy your own later.

screens.prompt: The family will pay ₹18,000. You must first spend ₹8,000 on flour, boxes and stands. How should you ask them to pay?

options.label: Ask for half now and half on the day
Ask for the full amount after the wedding
Offer ₹2,000 off if they pay it all now

screens.why: Right. Half of ₹18,000 is ₹9,000. That's enough to pay the ₹8,000 you need first. Remember the gym deal from Unit 1: before taking a big order, check how much money you need before the customer pays.

wrong.a: Then you must spend ₹8,000 of your own money and wait for payment. Remember Unit 1: ask for some money in advance. Half now is ₹9,000, enough to cover the ₹8,000.
wrong.c: You would lose ₹2,000 when you don't need to. Instead, ask for half in advance. That's ₹9,000, enough to cover the ₹8,000 you must spend first.

screens.text: Chain A takes 7 days. Chain B's jobs take 4, 3 and 1 days. Both start together. The critical path is chain ___, taking ___ days.
screens.why: Exactly. Chain B takes 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 days, longer than Chain A's 7 days. So B is your critical path. Keep extra days for it, and buy ready-made things if making them could delay you.

summary: Critical path: the longest chain of jobs that must wait for each other. It sets your finish date.
Speeding up a job off the critical path doesn't move the finish date.
Hofstadter's law: things take longer than you plan. Add spare days, and buy ready-made anything that could make you late.

cards.front: Job A takes 8 days. Jobs B then C take 3 and 2 days. They run side by side. When can you finish?
cards.back: The longest chain decides: 8 days. That's the critical path.

cards.front: A part from far away may make you late. What should you do?
options: Buy or rent it nearby, and make it yourself later
cards.back: Buy ready-made anything that could make you late.

cards.front: A job took 4, 5 and 7 days before. How long do you plan?
cards.back: Hofstadter's law: things take longer than you plan. Plan for the slowest.

sources.label: A well-planned and efficient Delhi Metro: tracing 16-year journey (ThePrint)
